_readme: Which document owns which subject. Checked by tools/tests/test_subject_ownership.py, on every ref. A subject declared anywhere but its owner fails, unless the ref is recorded in divergence_ledger.json. Detector kinds are implemented in subjects.py; a subject with no detector cannot be enforced and is rejected by the suite. Exemptions are narrow on purpose: execution records are append-only evidence and decision records must be able to name what they retired. Handoff documents are not exempt — SESSION_STATE on PR #3 declares an execution order, and that is a finding, not an allowance.

benchmark execution order.why: Three documents declared three different orders 14 minutes apart on 2026-08-31; the first two were violated by what actually ran.

claim and result state vocabulary.why: Three vocabularies were in force at once; recording CLM-0004 after R3 required mixing two of them.

benchmark identity and state table.why: Two identifier schemes named the same benchmarks; RESEARCH_TO_CLAIM_MAP used both in one table row.

corpus reconciliation exit criterion.why: Two documents carried an exit criterion; R1-R3 all ran while it said PARTIAL.
